description:
At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.

Responsibilities 
 

 
 Design and implement methods for adapting generative robot policies using techniques such as reinforcement learning, imitation learning, agentic tool use, and related methods.



 
 Develop methods that enable generative robot policies to improve through ongoing interaction with people and the environment, using signals such as demonstrations, interventions, preference feedback, learned rewards, and other human-driven signals.



 
 Develop rollout-based learning and exploration strategies that enable robots to efficiently and safely gather useful experience, leveraging multimodal data from demonstrations, teleoperation, interventions, and on-policy rollouts. In both simulation and on real robot hardware.



 
 Collaborate across teams in perception, control, foundation models, and ML infrastructure to deploy scalable and reproducible research systems.



 
 Publish research outcomes and contribute to the open robotics and embodied AI communities.






Qualifications 
 

 
 Ph.D. or M.S. in Robotics, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, or a related field, or equivalent applied research experience.



 
 Strong background in reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or closely related robot-learning methods.



 
 Strong proficiency with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX and robotics simulation environments such as IsaacLab or MuJoCo.



 
 Experience with policy adaptation, continual learning, preference learning, or related learning problems in embodied settings.



 
 Strong coding and experimental skills with an emphasis on reproducibility and rigorous evaluation.



 
 Prior robotics experience with real-world hardware and ML-based robot deployments.



 
 Publications in top-tier conferences such as CoRL, RSS, NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ICRA, or CVPR.






Bonus Qualifications 
 

 
 Experience with human-in-the-loop robot learning (e.g., DAgger), preference learning, reward learning, or RLHF/RLAIF.



 
 Prior work on generative robot policies or VLAs such as π0.5, GR00T, or related models.



 
 Experience building or managing robot data collection or replay infrastructure.



 
 Familiarity with real-world robot platforms such as YAMs, Kinova, humanoids, or mobile manipulators.
